literal: Every time knowing, ignorance having seen, it is like that indeed, passion, every time embracing, fine-jewel-woman with.
translation: Just as learning more only reveals the vastness of one's own ignorance, passion feels entirely new every time I embrace this woman with fine jewels.
modern: அறிவு வளர வளர நம் அறியாமை நமக்குத் தெரிவது போல, சிறந்த அணிகலன்களை அணிந்த இவளைத் தழுவும்போதெல்லாம் காமம் புதிதாகத் தோன்றுகிறது.
explanation: This couplet draws a striking parallel between the pursuit of knowledge and the experience of physical love. As a person learns more ('அறிதோறு'), they begin to realize the immense scale of what they still do not know ('அறியாமை'). In the exact same way, every time the lover embraces the woman ('செறிதோறும்'), he discovers new, unfathomable depths of passion ('காமம்'). The word 'சேயிழை' literally means 'red or fine jewels', but here it is used as a metonymy to refer to the beautiful woman wearing them. The comparison beautifully illustrates how true love, like true knowledge, is inexhaustible and always feels fresh.
